speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) how the Ministry assesses Singapore's economic, social and cultural status (ESCS) slope ranking of second out of 79 in the Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) systems, given that comparable high-performing systems such as Japan and Korea rank significantly lower; (b) what specific measures target a reduction in this slope; and (c) what progress is expected.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Education)
text: This differential gives rise to the steeper slope.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Education)
text: One simplistic way to flatten the slope is to stop our higher-performing students from doing so well.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Education)
text: But that is not educationally sound and goes against our education philosophy of helping all students to develop to their full potential.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: I think one of the concerns is, what the economic, social and cultural status (ESCS) slope implies or suggests is whether performance is driven by income or at least affected by income.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: I am not saying that it is caused by income, but whether there is a strong correlation between SES and performance.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: So, it is not about capping potential, but whether or not the folks from higher SES backgrounds have more opportunities, and because of that, that leads to that increase in academic performance.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: And my second supplementary question, it is related to the one I had asked before – whether or not this is an indicator that MOE will look into tracking because it can give a sense of whether the measures that have been implemented are working or not.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: I think the first question was more of a comment, I did not really catch the specific question, the first part of it.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh
text: Yes, it is more of a comment in response to her point about capping potential of high performance.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh
text: So, the Minister of State was talking about one way of flattening the slope would be to lower the top end.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh
text: But I do not think that necessarily means depriving people of opportunities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh
text: I think what it suggests is that there might be a certain group of people with more opportunities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh
text: And because of that, that gives them the chances to do better and hence, you see that the stronger relationship between ESCS and performance.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh
text: So, it is maybe putting forth a different interpretation of the data, and likewise, with the different interpretation, there could be different policy implications as well.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh
text: Specifically, my question is whether MOE would consider that different interpretation and how that might change the policy.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: Absolutely, I thank the Member for the clarification.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: I do not think I heard a specific question, but if the question is about whether I am aware of the research, well, after today, I definitely will be.
